content:
{a}Every mornin' 'bout seven o'clock there were {E}twenty terriers a-workin' on the rock.
The {a}boss comes along and he says: "Keep still! And {E}come down heavy on the cast-iron drill!"
And {a}drill ye {E}terriers, {a}drill! Drill ye {G}terriers, {a}drill! For it's work all day for the {E}sugar in your tay, down behind the railway. And {a}drill, ye {E}terriers, {a}drill! {E}And {a}blast! {E}And {a}fire!

/: G F E :/

Our boss was a fine man to the ground, but he married a lady, six-feet round.
She baked good bread and she baked it well, but she baked it hard as the coals in hell.

Our new foreman was Jim McCann. By god, he was a damn mean man.
Last week a premature blast went off, a mile in the sky went big Jim Goff.

The next time payday came around, a dollar short Jim Goff was found.
When he asked what for came this reply: "You're docked for the time you were up in the sky."
title: Drill ye terriers
info: Das Lied ist ein Arbeitslied und bezieht sich auf den Bau der amerikanischen Eisenbahnen im mittleren 19. Jahrhundert. Der Titel bezieht sich auf irische Arbeiter, die Löcher in den Felsen bohren, um Eisenbahntunnel auszusprengen. Es kann entweder "verweilen" (tarry) im Sinne von Verzögerung bedeuten oder auf Terrier-Hunde hinweisen, die ihre Beute aus dem Boden ausgraben, oder von dem französischen Wort für eine Bohrmaschine, tarière.
